title: China and Canada set out which financial links they will test next
summary: China and Canada have agreed how their joint financial working group will operate. The PBoC identifies three signatories: Governor Pan Gongsheng, Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne and Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem. The announcement gives the group a regular channel for cooperation across monetary and financial policy, supervision, financial markets, stability and cross-border flows. It follows the leaders’ January joint statement, an inaugural meeting in Beijing in April and a roundtable with financial institutions. The November step formalises the remit and the way the institutions will communicate.

The most concrete item for funding markets is a commitment to test and discuss using the recently renewed bilateral local-currency swap agreement. The parties welcome implementation by their central banks and will explore wider use of local currencies in bilateral trade and investment. The release gives no drawdown, amount used or terms on which a commercial bank could obtain liquidity. A test can clarify operational readiness even if no institution has an immediate funding need. Assessing actual use would require subsequent central bank disclosures.

The announcement also identifies two directions for debt-market access. The parties welcome eligible Canadian institutions issuing renminbi-denominated panda bonds in China. Separately, Canada welcomes and supports China’s intention to issue renminbi green sovereign bonds in the Canadian market. The second proposal concerns a different issuer and market from a Canadian borrower issuing in China. Neither passage names a completed transaction, an issue size or a pricing date. The distinction matters for anyone trying to translate the announcement into expected bond supply or demand for currency hedges.

The working group has already conducted technical exchanges on panda bonds, cross-border payment efficiency and financial crime controls. It also plans dialogue on financial technology and global financial governance, encouragement of two-way investment and discussion of green and sustainable finance in multilateral settings. These are channels through which the institutions can resolve practical questions. The evidence of market impact would come from changes in settlement activity, issuance and access to funding after implementation.

questions.question: What would demonstrate that the currency swap can supply usable liquidity?
questions.detail: Testing is an explicit objective, but the announcement gives no transaction amount, tenor or pass-through to banks. Look for notices from both central banks distinguishing an operational test from a drawing, and setting out eligible recipients and settlement arrangements. Those details determine whether market participants can treat the arrangement as a practical source of local-currency funding during periods of stress.

questions.question: Which proposed bond channel reaches the market first?
questions.detail: Track Canadian issuers’ panda bond registrations and individual offerings separately from any Chinese sovereign green bond documentation in Canada. For each, check currency, maturity, issue size, price and investor allocation. The distinction matters because an announcement about access for commercial or institutional issuers has a different bearing on the investable bond supply from a dated sovereign funding transaction.

questions.question: Do payment arrangements lead to more local-currency settlement?
questions.detail: The group has discussed payment efficiency and plans to explore wider local-currency use. Neither gives a starting share of bilateral trade settled in local currencies. Examine subsequent settlement data, payment charges and processing times alongside trade volumes. A currency share that rises after an identifiable change in costs would give more information about adoption than an increase in trade alone.

limitation: The PBoC announcement describes the agreed work programme. It does not reproduce the operating standards or the swap agreement.
